slides.headline: The Women’s World Cup is getting its biggest stage yet
slides.subline: **FIFA picked the 2031 and 2035 hosts.** The 2031 tournament grows to 48 teams.
slides.credit: U.S. Department of State / Public domain

slides.body: The **United States** will co-host with **Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica**. The bid offers [[20 venues]]: 14 in the US, four in Mexico, plus San José and Kingston.
A United Kingdom bid led by England was ratified, with [[19 venues]] across England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales, including **Wembley**.
The 2031 tournament will have [[48 teams]] for the first time. The 2027 event in Brazil has 32. More teams means more countries get a shot at the stage.
Both bids passed by acclamation, with **no rival bids**. FIFA’s president and the winning candidates pledged to reinvest all profits in [[women’s soccer]].
Four host nations in 2031, and a UK final in 2035. Which match would you travel to see? Tell us below.
